content:
The threshold energy for the high-energy gamma-ray to pair produce with a CMB photon is given by the head-on collision condition: \(4 E_{\gamma} \epsilon \geq (2 m_e c^2)^2\), where \(\epsilon = 10^{-3} \text{ eV}\) is the average CMB photon energy and \(m_e c^2 = 0.511 \text{ MeV} = 5.11 \times 10^5 \text{ eV}\). Solving for \(E_{\gamma}\):

\[
E_{\gamma} \approx \frac{(m_e c^2)^2}{\epsilon} = \frac{(0.511 \times 10^6 \text{ eV})^2}{10^{-3} \text{ eV}} = \frac{0.261 \times 10^{12} \text{ eV}^2}{10^{-3} \text{ eV}} = 2.61 \times 10^{14} \text{ eV} = 2.6 \times 10^5 \text{ GeV}.
\]

This corresponds to option (B).

Answer: B
